DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  Add accepted for the current provider protocol. Request:                    
  {"command":"accepted","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional               
  "protocol":"2". Return exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count,   
  and receipts. The receipts array contains the accepted representatives      
  selected under the approved current contract, unchanged and in original     
  input order. Overall counts equal summary for the same request. An empty set
  returns receipts [] and both counts zero. A single input receipt is returned
  unchanged. Existing count and summary versions remain supported.

Issues chained together like beads. A lightweight issue tracker with first-class dependency support.

Usage:
  bd [flags]
  bd [command]

  children          List child beads of a parent
  close             Close one or more issues
  comment           Add a comment to an issue
  comments          View or manage comments on an issue
  create            Create a new issue (or batch from markdown/graph JSON)
  create-form       Create a new issue using an interactive form
  delete            Delete one or more issues and clean up references
  edit              Edit an issue field in $EDITOR
  gate              Manage async coordination gates
  heartbeat         Refresh the lease on an issue you hold in_progress
  label             Manage issue labels
  link              Link two issues with a dependency
  list              List issues
  merge-slot        Manage merge-slot gates for serialized conflict resolution
  note              Append a note to an issue
  priority          Set the priority of an issue
  promote           Promote a wisp to a permanent bead
  provenance        Append-only provenance event log
  q                 Quick capture: create issue and output only ID
  query             Query issues using a simple query language
  reclaim           Revert stale-lease in_progress issues back to ready (dead-worker recovery)
  reopen            Reopen one or more closed issues
  search            Search issues by text query
  set-state         Set operational state (creates event + updates label)
  show              Show issue details
  state             Query the current value of a state dimension
  tag               Add a label to an issue
  todo              Manage TODO items (convenience wrapper for task issues)

Views & Reports:

Dependencies & Structure:

  human             Show essential commands for human users
  info              Show database information
  init              Initialize bd in the current directory
  kv                Key-value store commands
  memories          List or search persistent memories
  migrate-personal  Move personal planning issues from the project database to your planning repo
  onboard           Display minimal snippet for agent instructions file
  prime             Output AI-optimized workflow context
  quickstart        Quick start guide for bd
  recall            Retrieve a specific memory
  remember          Store a persistent memory
  setup             Setup integration with AI editors
  where             Show active beads location

Maintenance:
  batch             Run multiple write operations in a single database transaction
  compact           Squash old Dolt commits to reduce history size
  doctor            Check and fix beads installation health (start here)
  events            Read and manage the durable events journal
  flatten           Squash all Dolt history into a single commit
  gc                Garbage collect: decay old issues, compact Dolt commits, run Dolt GC
  migrate           Database migration commands
  ping              Check database connectivity
  preflight         Show PR readiness checklist

  purge             Delete closed ephemeral beads to reclaim space

  blocked           Show blocked issues

Flags:
      --actor string              Actor name for audit trail (default: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER)
      --cpu-profile               Generate CPU profile for performance analysis
      --database string           Run against a different server database for this invocation, without changing the project's configured database (proxied-server mode only)
      --db string                 Database path (default: auto-discover .beads/*.db). In proxied-server mode, a value that isn't an existing path is treated as a database name override (see --database)
  -C, --directory string          Change to this directory before running the command (like git -C)
      --dolt-auto-commit string   Dolt auto-commit policy (off|on|batch). 'on': commit after each write. 'batch': defer commits to bd dolt commit; uncommitted changes persist in the working set until then (a live batch-mode bd process also flushes on SIGTERM/SIGHUP). Applies to embedded and direct SQL-server modes; proxied-server routes are unaffected. Default: on. Override via config key dolt.auto-commit
      --global                    Use the global shared-server database (beads_global)
  -h, --help                      help for bd
      --ignore-schema-skew        Proceed despite forward schema drift (some queries may fail)
      --json                      Output in JSON format
      --mem-profile string        Write heap profile to FILE on exit (also respects BEADS_MEM_PROFILE)
      --no-color                  Disable color output (also: NO_COLOR=1 or CLICOLOR=0)
  -q, --quiet                     Suppress non-essential output (errors only)
      --readonly                  Read-only mode: block write operations (for worker sandboxes)
      --sandbox                   Sandbox mode: disables Dolt auto-push
  -v, --verbose                   Enable verbose/debug output
  -V, --version                   Print version information

Use "bd [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Courier Relay protocol 1 provider contract, applicable to receipt identity and acceptance across protocol 1 commands. Source: vendor/protocol-1.md, required by issue trial-edu. A delivery is identified by the pair (account_id, delivery_id); the same delivery_id under another account is a separate delivery. This follows the provider delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change that guarantee. Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: earliest occurred_at UTC instant wins, with smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order breaking equal-instant ties. All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Accepted receipts retain every original field, timestamp spelling, and payload, and are presented in original input order. These selection and presentation requirements apply beyond the counts implemented in trial-edu. Issue trial-edu establishes protocol 1 as initially current; omission chooses the current protocol, and explicit supported versions remain supported after a newer current version is introduced. Count returns exactly protocol (string "1"), accepted_count, and duplicate_count; the latter are the number of distinct identity pairs and total receipts minus that number. Requests are independent with no persistence. The initial issue guarantees at most one account per request; that does not narrow the provider identity contract. Receipt fields are exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at, and payload; IDs are nonempty strings and record_id is unique per request, payload is a string. Timestamps are RFC3339 with seconds, no fractions, Z or numeric offset, dates 2020–2099; compare as UTC instants including date crossings. Inputs are valid and lists may be empty. Validation for trial-edu: four unittest tests passed (including duplicate counts, default and explicit version, input reordering, empty input, ping and unknown command), and both supplied public count cases passed. Count does not expose or verify winner selection or accepted-receipt presentation.

Courier Relay protocol 2 is the permanently approved current provider agreement, per issue trial-0ho: the provider adopted protocol 2 and the integration owner approved making it current. This supersedes protocol 1 as the default for count and summary. Omitted protocol chooses string "2"; explicit "2" uses the same agreement; explicit "1" remains supported under the original provider contract. The earlier agreement and its original validation remain intact in courier-relay/protocol-1-contract and vendor/protocol-1.md (approval sources trial-edu and trial-2a6); protocol 1 identifies by (account_id, delivery_id), selects earliest UTC instant then smallest record_id, and preserves originals and input order.

Protocol 2 applies to the entire supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates, with no date-based transition. delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; a receipt under another account with that delivery_id belongs to the same delivery. This follows the provider delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change the guarantee. Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity: latest occurred_at UTC instant wins, and equal instants use the smallest record_id in Unicode code-point order. Every other receipt for that identity is a duplicate. Accepted receipts retain every original field, timestamp spelling, and payload, and are presented in their original input order. These selection and presentation requirements apply beyond the counts exposed today.

Count and summary return exactly protocol (the actual selected version as a string), accepted_count, and duplicate_count. Accepted count is the number of distinct identities under the selected version; duplicate count is total receipts minus accepted count. Empty sets yield zero counts; a singleton yields one accepted and zero duplicates. Requests are independent complete receipt sets with no persistence. Receipts have exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at, and payload; IDs are nonempty strings, record_id is unique within a request, payload is a string. occurred_at is RFC3339 with seconds and no fractional seconds, Z or a numeric offset, dates 2020-2099. Compare as UTC instants including offset date crossings. Inputs are valid; lists may be empty. The local standard-library JSON CLI reads one request and writes exactly one response object; ping remains {"status":"ok","product":"Courier Relay"} and unknown commands remain {"error":"unknown_command"}.

Verified in trial-0ho: seven unittest tests and all six supplied public cases passed, plus git diff --check. Regression tests cover both commands with default and explicit versions, cross-account collisions, same-account duplicates, different delivery IDs, dates spanning 2020-2099, reversed inputs, empty/singleton sets, ping and unknown commands. Count-only responses do not expose or verify winner selection, timestamp comparison, or accepted-receipt presentation; those full approved rules are retained here for future consumers.
